articles.title: Tielemans in the 125th Minute. Belgium Came Back From the Dead in Seattle — and NRIs in the Pacific Northwest Had Front-Row Seats.
articles.excerpt: Down 2-0 with four minutes left, Belgium staged the World Cup's most dramatic comeback yet. Youri Tielemans scored twice, including a 125th-minute penalty after a controversial VAR call, to sink Senegal 3-2 in extra time at Lumen Field.
articles.image_caption: Youri Tielemans in Belgium colors during the March 2026 friendly against the United States
articles.nri_angle: Seattle's 100,000+ Indian tech community had front-row seats to the World Cup's most dramatic comeback — and Belgium's Round of 16 match is also at Lumen Field, keeping the tournament in the Pacific Northwest NRI heartland.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kane Scores Twice, Passes Pelé. England Survive DR Congo and Head to the Azteca.
articles.excerpt: Harry Kane's 75th and 86th minute goals rescued England from the brink of elimination in Atlanta, pushing him past Pelé's all-time World Cup record. Next up: co-hosts Mexico in one of football's most hostile arenas.
articles.image_caption: Harry Kane in action for England — the Bayern Munich striker now has 13 World Cup goals
